Are there secrets to being a good presenter? Some folks consistently have amazing presentations while others have rotten ones despite all the world of practice. What tricks do you use to turn your presentation into something that people remember and enjoy, especially in case of academic presentations?

Is there a particular way of talking that makes one sound more interesting?
How can one become a better presenter and make their presentations more impactful?

Major in literature and take some speech classes.

College really helps you do anything.

I make them pleasing to the eyes and simple to the mind. I also give eye contact to the whole group and use my body language to help portray what I’m trying to say.

Of course the most important part is preparing well and practicing.

A secrete might be, trying to implement emotion into you presentation. What I mean by that is trying to impact the group emotionally about your topic.

I follow the simplistic approach. My favorite design is no template, with Roboto as my Title and Body font in wide screen mode. I set my background to R: 250, G: 250, B: 250, which is a very light grey. My title font size is 44 and body is 36. This keeps the slides clean and very clean. Not to mention it makes readability very high.

With the clutter gone, it is down to your matter and your talk; people can focus on that instead now.

I am not so sure about making your presentation emotional, it may work in some cases but it may work against you in other presentations...like may be your job talk.

Start be believing in your presentation. You have to sell the idea to your self before you can try and sell it to others. I'm not sure how your presentations work, but mine are an active dialogue were an expert in their field gives info to group and the group can ask questions. The people who do a good job at these know their shit and how to respond to a question and keep rolling their presentation without missing a beat. A good way to practice is to find a debate group or mock election group and just practice talking to people. Hope this helped.

Edit: forgot to say: Speak in a tone that is natural but everyone can still here you. This is huge and is right next to believeing what your saying.

In my limited talking experience I find that several things help engage an audience. 1) Eye contact is very important and you want to use notes as little as you can. The more time you spend looking at them the more they feel like you are talking to them. Don't focus on one spot though...you need to look all over, and if you can try not to focus on anything at all. just do the head movements and leave your concentration for the speaking. 2) Use small hand gestures. You don't want to be flailing about but you also don't want to be standing still the whole time. 3) Have proof for any claims that you say. If you just keep rattling off stuff without proof or logical explanation people will become less interested and more skeptical. On the flip side if you make claims and prove it people will stay focused for longer. 4) If you can control it.... the size of an audience can be very critical and can make or break a performer/speaker, you want a size that is small enough that it won't unsettle you but not too small that it will discourage you. 5) Don't stay on one piece of information for too long because it will get boring. approach the topic from multiple directions to keep people's attention

I realize that this post goes against what I said in point #3 but it is almost 4 in the morning and I am writing this all offhand....I hope this helps a little. Edit: A cpl of forgotten words
Lot's of music, and a fog machine never hurts.

I believe watching more TED talks (good ones) can help.
Get well prepared and have full understanding of what you are going to talk about. Then believe in yourself and be confident. Stand straight and speak clearly. Smile.

I think some TED talks like the power posing help you with presentations, TED presentations are a very different ballgame I think. They have a teleprompter in front of them, a large timer, a professionally created presentation and so on. I think a lot of those luxuries aren't available for the average presentation, like say...your job talk.

It'll depend on your crowd/audience, but the best way to handle eye contact is to pick three people, one to the left, centre and right. Then make eye contact with those three people throughout the presentation. Focus solely on those three people, nobody else exists. Imagine you're only giving a presentation to those three people and nobody else. This should help conquer nerves and also sorts out the eye contact problem easily (as you'll be focusing at specific spots across the room).
Have something meaningful to present. Its the message, not the media.

The biggest thing for me is clear and confident speaking. Don't look at the floor, or at the screen. Look at the people you are speaking to. Stop and think about what you want to say instead of using filler words like uhm etc. These two things make a huge difference between presentations I tolerate and presentations I'm engaged in.
Think about it from the audience's perspective.
